interactions.label: In the clinical vignette, which feature of the patient's morning stiffness most

params.question: In the clinical vignette, which feature of the patient's morning stiffness most reliably points to an inflammatory rather than a degenerative cause?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Bilateral involvement can occur in both inflammatory and degenerative arthritis (e.g., bilateral Heberden's nodes in OA). The behaviour of stiffness — its duration and response to activity — is the more reliable discriminator.

answers.text: It lasts more than 60 minutes and improves with activity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Prolonged morning stiffness (>60 minutes) that eases with activity is the hallmark of inflammatory arthritis. In osteoarthritis, stiffness is brief (<30 minutes) and typically worsens with use.

answers.text: It is associated with fatigue and weight loss

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Systemic features like fatigue and weight loss support an inflammatory aetiology but are not specific to the stiffness pattern. The key discriminator is stiffness duration (>60 min) and improvement with activity.
PIP joints can be affected in both rheumatoid arthritis and nodal osteoarthritis (Bouchard's nodes). Joint distribution alone does not distinguish the two; the stiffness pattern is more reliable.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key discriminator is the behaviour of morning stiffness: >60 minutes duration improving with activity points to inflammation; brief stiffness (<30 min) worsening with use points to degeneration.
Well done. Morning stiffness >60 minutes improving with activity is the single most important bedside clue to inflammatory arthritis.

interactions.label: NSAIDs are sufficient to prevent joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis becau

params.question: NSAIDs are sufficient to prevent joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis because they reduce synovial inflammation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is a critical misconception. Although NSAIDs reduce symptoms of inflammation, they do not halt the autoimmune process driving pannus formation and joint erosion. Only DMARDs — which target the immune mechanism — prevent structural damage.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. NSAIDs reduce pain and swelling but do NOT prevent joint destruction. Only DMARDs target the underlying autoimmune cascade (CD4+ T-cell activation, cytokine production, pannus formation) and are truly disease-modifying.

interactions.label: Which combination of hand examination findings best distinguishes rheumatoid art

params.question: Which combination of hand examination findings best distinguishes rheumatoid arthritis from both osteoarthritis and psoriatic arthritis?

answers.text: Hard bony enlargement of DIP joints with crepitus on movement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes osteoarthritis — Heberden's nodes are hard, bony DIP enlargements. RA produces boggy synovial thickening (not bony) and characteristically spares the DIP joints.

answers.text: Boggy synovial thickening of MCPs and PIPs with DIP sparing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Boggy (soft, warm) synovial thickening distinguishes RA from OA's hard bony nodes, while DIP sparing distinguishes RA from PsA which characteristically involves the DIP joints.

answers.text: Asymmetrical swelling of DIP joints with nail pitting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This pattern is characteristic of psoriatic arthritis, which involves DIPs asymmetrically and is associated with nail changes (pitting, onycholysis). RA is symmetrical and spares DIPs.

answers.text: Symmetrical MCP swelling with DIP involvement and subcutaneous nodules

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While rheumatoid nodules are indeed an RA feature, DIP involvement contradicts the diagnosis. RA characteristically spares DIP joints — this is one of the most reliable bedside differentiators.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the two key differentiators: boggy synovial thickening (vs hard bony enlargement in OA) and DIP sparing (vs DIP involvement in PsA and OA). Together they point to RA.
Excellent analysis. Boggy synovial thickening (not bony) plus DIP sparing is the two-feature combination that separates RA from both OA and PsA at the bedside.

interactions.label: A young man presents with chronic low back pain and stiffness that improves with

params.question: A young man presents with chronic low back pain and stiffness that improves with exercise. He is RF-negative and HLA-B27 positive. Which radiological finding would confirm the most likely diagnosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Periarticular osteoporosis of MCPs is an early radiological sign of rheumatoid arthritis, which is seropositive (RF/anti-CCP) and affects peripheral joints symmetrically — not the axial skeleton.

answers.text: Bilateral sacroiliac joint fusion with syndesmophytes forming a bamboo spine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This profile — axial inflammatory pain improving with exercise, RF-negative, HLA-B27 positive — is classic ankylosing spondylitis. Sacroiliac fusion and bamboo spine are its pathognomonic radiological findings.

answers.text: Pencil-in-cup deformity of the distal interphalangeal joints

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pencil-in-cup deformity is the characteristic radiological finding of psoriatic arthritis, which typically presents with asymmetrical peripheral joint involvement and associated skin and nail changes.

answers.text: Joint space narrowing with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes osteoarthritis — a degenerative process. The clinical features here (young age, inflammatory back pain improving with exercise, HLA-B27 positivity) point to an inflammatory spondyloarthropathy, not OA.

overallFeedback.feedback: The clinical profile — young man, inflammatory back pain improving with exercise, RF-negative, HLA-B27 positive — points to ankylosing spondylitis. Its pathognomonic radiology is bilateral sacroiliac fusion and syndesmophytes forming a bamboo spine.

Well done. You correctly integrated history (young male, axial inflammatory pain), serology (RF-negative, HLA-B27 positive), and imaging (sacroiliac fusion, bamboo spine) to confirm ankylosing spondylitis.
